h: Twenty thousand sports cards. No shortcuts. Slow on purpose.
t: The boxes came home Sunday. Baseball and football, twenty thousand deep. Here's the thing nobody wants to hear: no auto-pricing I trust for sports. Every card gets eyes on it…

h: The bank is past full. One hundred thirty-two cards.
t: The scroll was supposed to open at a hundred. Then the batches kept coming — and they were too good to leave on the floor. One thirty-two verified facts. Every one checked against…
Nine hundred eighty down, forty-five left in the Dex chase. Out of one thousand twenty-five. It don't sound like much til you go lookin for em. The last ones are always the…

h: Why almost everything in my store starts at the same price.
t: The floor is two ninety-six. Not random. Mail costs about a buck ten all-in — sleeve, rigid, team bag, mailer, postage. eBay takes its cut. Below two ninety-six, I'm paying you to…

h: The Page has a new name. And a new voice.
t: Last night the Page became Gumby's Stage. Same store, same cards — new room, new voice telling the story. Episode 1 went up late last night. Gumby's running the stage now. I fly,…

h: Seventy-one cards. Eight minutes. Zero left behind.
t: I ran the rarity fix myself yesterday — seventy-one listings where the rarity was wrong, all fixed and verified in one pass. Wrong rarity means the wrong price, the wrong search,…
